analysis:
The supplied units cover docs/architecture/inference.md only, in head-side excerpts of lines 798-1640. The patch adds documentation at lines 872-878 (out-of-order measurement freshness) and 1123-1183 (TTFT admission estimator corrections). The base-side change at 2030 and the head-side change at 2098 fall outside the supplied excerpts.

No code, key handling, attestation, cache-storage, encryption or coordinator-contract behavior changes in these units. The text describes provider-local admission and deadline estimation: freshness anchored to the newest observation, per-step decode pricing, an idle-rate bound on isolated prefill, and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 rollback.

Security-relevant observations:
- The new env toggle is a performance/admission control. The doc says deadline profiles reject unrecognized performance-affecting DARKBLOOM_* settings via DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification. Whether the new variable is covered by that allowlist or exemption is not visible here. If it is not, a qualified profile could be applied with altered estimators; this is an unverified contract.
- The estimator changes affect availability and DoS posture (T-010, T-029). They could admit work that misses its deadline, but the doc states that physical admission, memory reservation and elapsed deadline expiry still apply. I see no concrete regression.
- The measurements are numeric only and the doc names no new data exposure. This does not touch the T-041 cache oracle (no cache TTL, key or scope change), the T-053 authorization binding, or the A-003/A-015 key custody.
- The prefix-cache text is unchanged in the visible excerpt; the 30-minute TTL statements in the canonical model are not contradicted.

The actual source for AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift and the CBv2 deadline admission is not supplied, so doc accuracy against code is unverified. That is a coverage limit, not evidence of a vulnerability.
